standard_prerequisites.name: Comparability graph of a partially ordered set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given a partially ordered set, its comparability graph has the elements as vertices and an undirected edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding elements are comparable; the article's own description is retained at source lines 117-120.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the object that the proof constructs twice on the disjoint pairs of a subtree system, and whose union must reproduce the disjointness graph of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The partition number p(G) and the cover number c(G)
standard_prerequisites.statement: p(G) is the minimum m such that the edge set of G is the union of m edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs of G, and c(G) is the same number without the edge-disjointness requirement, so that p(G) is at least c(G); retained at source lines 128-129.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts c(G) <= p(G) <= 2, so both parameters and their mutual relation must be fixed before the statement can be read.

standard_prerequisites.name: Disjointness graph of a system of subtrees
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a tree T and a system F of subtrees of T, the disjointness graph has F as its vertex set and an edge between two subtrees exactly when they are disjoint; a graph is co-triangulated when it arises in this way, and the article records at source lines 276 and 278 that the complements of these graphs are the chordal, alias triangulated, graphs.
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the graph G of the counted theorem with the disjointness graph of F, which is the graph the two constructed partial orders must partition.

core_obligations: Fix a tree T, a system F of subtrees of T and a root r of T, and note that every subtree A of F has a unique vertex closest to r, its root (source lines 319-323).

Define the first relation on disjoint pairs: A is claimed to precede B when the path from the root of B to r contains the root of A; verify antisymmetry, and verify transitivity by showing that the path from the root of C to r contains the path from the root of B to r and hence the root of A, and that the root of B separates A and C so that they are disjoint (source lines 324-334).
Define the lexicographic partial order on the set of finite sequences of natural numbers, restricted to pairs of sequences neither of which is a prefix of the other (source lines 337-339).
Define the labelling of the vertices of T by sequences, recursively from the root, choosing an arbitrary order on the children and using the child index as the next entry (source lines 341-349).

Establish the dictionary between the two orders: for disjoint subtrees A and B with roots a and b, A precedes B in the first order exactly when the label of a is a prefix of the label of b (source lines 350-351).

Define the second relation on disjoint pairs that are incomparable in the first order: A precedes B when the label of a is lexicographically before the label of b; verify antisymmetry and transitivity, using that no label of a is a prefix of the label of c and that prefixes of vertex labels lie lexicographically between them, so that A and C are disjoint (source lines 353-371).

Conclude that the comparability graphs of the two relations partition the disjointness graph of F, whence the partition number of the co-triangulated graph is at most two and therefore the cover number is at most two as well (source lines 372-373).

proof_roadmap.step: Root the tree T and assign to each subtree of F its root, the vertex closest to r.
Define the first order by comparing subtree roots along the paths to r and prove that it is a partial order on the disjoint pairs.
Define the lexicographic order on finite sequences of natural numbers for incomparable pairs.
Label the vertices of T by sequences and identify the first order with the prefix relation of the labels of the subtree roots.
Define the second order on the pairs incomparable in the first order and check antisymmetry and transitivity.
Use the prefix properties of the vertex labels to show that the two subtrees related in the second order are disjoint.
Conclude that the two comparability graphs partition the disjointness graph.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem co-triangulated（源 313-316 行，证明 319-373 行，共 55 行）：对共三角图的集合（即树 T 的子树系的互斥图）证明 c(G)<=p(G)<=2，也就是要把它的边集恰好剖成两个可比图。关键操作不是例行核验：作者必须先把结点按「离根最近」给每个子树定出根，再用「B 的根到 r 的路径是否含 A 的根」造出第一个偏序，并验证传递性时用到「B 的根把 A 与 C 分开因而二者互斥」这一几何事实（324-334 行）；随后还要处理第一个偏序下不可比的互斥对，为此引入 N^{<=N} 上的字典序与顶点标号 ψ，并证明第一个偏序恰好等于标号的前缀关系（337-351 行），再用前缀性质证明第二个偏序的传递性并推出结论的两棵子树互斥（353-371 行）。难点在于两个偏序必须互补地覆盖互斥图的所有边，这要求对同一树结构下的两类互斥对给出两套相容的序，任何一套的传递性都需要独立论证；原文位置在证明的 329-334 行与 358-371 行。

The source preamble cannot be retained as it stands: it loads rawfonts, psfrag, verbatim, tikz with several libraries, hyperref with the pagebackref option and a dvi driver option for graphicx, none of which the retained body spans use, and it redefines backref commands that only exist because of that hyperref option. The retained preamble file therefore carries, line for line, source line 2, source line 3, source line 4, source line 16, source line 17, the theorem declarations of source lines 20-30 and the author macro definitions of source lines 32-41; the only textual change anywhere is the removal of the dvipdfm driver option from the graphicx line, because the assembly forces the xelatex engine. No new macro, package or declaration was introduced.
No retained line contains a citation: the sentences of the article that cite Dilworth, Mirsky, Gavril, Walter and the surveys are deliberately not retained, so the material carries no bibliography.
The article's theorems gensplit, bipline, unit, loglog and ub, its lemma rec and its proposition H9 are not counted here and are not used as premises.
